notes.title: BATTLEZONE®: COMBAT COMMANDER LAUNCHES MARCH 1ST 2018

notes.title: Battlezone: Combat Commander - Coming soon to Steam!
notes.notes:
[h1]BATTLEZONE® COMBAT COMMANDER REMASTERS THE CLASSIC FPS-RTS[/h1]

[img]https://i.imgur.com/BB374kf.jpg[/img]

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QB9eqiT_a7c&feature=youtu.be
[b]Independent UK developer and publisher Rebellion® is delighted to reveal BATTLEZONE® COMBAT COMMANDER, deploying to PC in 2018.[/b]

[img]https://i.imgur.com/PydNAYq.jpg[/img]
 
After Rebellion®'s TIGA Award-nominated remaster of Battlezone® (1998), many fans of the pioneering FPS-RTS hybrid asked for its acclaimed sequel, Battlezone® II: Combat Commander, to receive the same treatment. 
 
Developed by Big Boat Interactive and published by Rebellion®, [b]BATTLEZONE® COMBAT COMMANDER[/b] remasters Battlezone® II with slick new visuals, mod support for the game's two-decade old modding scene, cross-play online multiplayer between GOG & Steam for up to 14 players, achievements, cloud saves* and more.
 
A mysterious alien force threatens humanity itself. In this galaxy-wide war, you are in command of the resistance. Leading from the front, you take to the battlefield in thrilling first-person combat, piloting futuristic, customizable war machines including hover-tanks, colossal mech walkers, lightning-fast mortar-bikes and more.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/nNxBruJ.jpg[/img]
 
But you don't just fight from the front - you are in total command! A gripping singleplayer campaign will test your mettle as you learn to plot strategy, construct bases, form your armies, deploy defenses and call in airstrikes. Achieving victory is no mean feat in this remarkable blend of classic real-time strategy and first-person action. To save humanity, you must prove yourself a true combat commander! 
 
[h1]BATTLEZONE® COMBAT COMMANDER is coming to Steam in 2018.[/h1]
 
[b]Ahead of launch, fans can sign up for a chance to be a part of the game's closed beta at[/b] rebellion.com/bzcc 

[img]https://i.imgur.com/kAEwuSr.jpg[/img]
 
[b]About Rebellion®[/b]
[i]Founded in 1992, Rebellion® is one of Europe's leading independent game developers and publishers. Whether it's the breathtaking intensity of Sniper Elite 4, the face-hugging terror of Aliens vs. Predator or the grindhouse frenzy of Zombie Army Trilogy, the Oxford-based studio is known for creating stand-out games that thrill players.[/i] www.rebellion.com 
 
[b]About Big Boat Interactive[/b]
[i]Big Boat Interactive is an independent development studio based out of Los Angeles and run by game industry veteran Mike Arkin. Big Boat specializes in toy-connected mobile apps and remasters of classic games.[/i]

notes.title: Patch Notes - The Red Odyssey 24/08/2016!
notes.notes:
[h1]Mission Tuning[/h1]
[*][b]CH02 Mission[/b] - Stop bug that could cause unlimited spawning of hunters and reduce enemies in the waves to make less difficult at medium and higher difficulties.
[*][b]CH03 Mission[/b] - Fixed howitzers to work as intended and fixed mine field to be effective against player
[*][b]CH04 Mission[/b] - Add an abandoned enemy ship to make the retreat after discovery possible.
[*][b]CH08 Mission[/b] - Adds time to end so final VO completes
[*][b]CH09 Mission[/b] - Reduce difficulty.  The longer cover is maintained, the fewer enemies spawned when cover is finally left.  Enemies turrets also became single weapon turrets
[*][b]BD02 Mission[/b] - Reduced difficulty.
[*][b]BD03 Mission[/b] - Difficulty tuned, and several object spawning on top of each other issues fixed.
[*][b]BD04 Mission[/b] - Startup issues fixed.  Scavenger's shouldn't leave early which made it hard for new players to follow them. Final chase made more survivable while leaving the epic chase feeling intact.
[*][b]BD06 Mission[/b] - Enemy attack waves slightly reduced[/list]
[h1]General[/h1]
[list][*]A number of minor model fixes applied
[*]Fixed error with point lights.  Weapon fire shouldn't cause strange reverse shadows anymore.
[*]Chinese Scavenger emissive fixed (strange glow removed)
[*]TRO Music Added to game, and TRO missions play TRO sound files
[*]Fury hybrids no longer describe themselves as scavengers
[*]Black Dog weapon properly rotates only top to shoot now.
[*]CVHAUL adjusted how it holds items so it can't levitate itself
[*]Fixes BD constructor's description text.
[*]Non-playing sounds for several vehicles such as CH Constructor fixed.
[*]Fixed the CVAPC cockpit[/list]

[h1]The Patch also includes[/h1][list]
[*]Mod samples in Edit Mode fixed to be present and useful samples [/list]

notes.title: Battlezone 98 Mod Competition Winners
notes.notes:
[i]Firstly we’d like to say [b]a big thank you to everyone that entered the competition[/b], it’s been awesome to see new mods appearing on the store that have had such thought, time, and effort put in to them. We know the Battlezone 98 Redux community is a fantastic community, but the level of some of the mods that we saw was beyond anything we could have thought! As a thank you to everyone who entered a mod, we’re pleased to announce that you will all receive a Rebellion game of your choice! (Instructions of how to claim your game are at the bottom of this post)

Secondly, [b]we’d like to thank AMD Gaming[/b] for sponsoring this competition by generously providing us with a number of CPUs!

Lastly, we want to say [b]congratulations to our top 10 modders![/b] It was a difficult process to whittle down the entrants in to a top 10 as the standard of mods was extremely high, but below you can see who won and where you can find their mod! It’s hugely inspiring to see what you guys created and we hope inspires others to give it a go. In our eyes, everyone is a winner as they get to play the mods! So without further ado, we present the top 10![/i]

[h1]10.  The Space Race Aint Over! - Headcrab Addict[/h1][url=http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=737160374&searchtext=]LINK[/url]
A personal favourite of some members here at Rebellion, this mod allows the player to race against three other AI controlled vehicles in a map that feels very similar to the pod race on Tatooine! The developer has said that multiplayer is planned, and once this is available it will be a definite mod to try.[img]http://images.akamai.steamusercontent.com/ugc/264969860601444653/E046DDB0C828FF5F3CCCA3237631AB2C92B2D414/[/img]

[h1]9. American Pilot - CuddlyKitten[/h1][url=http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=734023236&searchtext=]LINK[/url]
Created as a result of the American faction not having an awesome looking outfit and the Chinese having a devious Red outfit, this mod gives your pilot a fresh space suit, complete with stars and stripes. Both the reasoning behind this and the design give this mod a definite space in our top 10![img]http://images.akamai.steamusercontent.com/ugc/275102315866471473/E7E48BF829356BF5E6AE4D2F2575674A7EC4109E/[/img]

[h1]8. More Realistic American Vehicles – Owenc3[/h1][url=http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=737128438&searchtext=]LINK[/url]
Continuing with the American theme, this mod overhauls all the American vehicles, giving them a fresh new lick of paint, including the token flag on the side. This mod also sees buildings being given a fresh new look, with awesome panels (possibly solar?) and gold touches. Bonus points also given for the overhaul to the Moonlander! [img]http://images.akamai.steamusercontent.com/ugc/1613797962857472414/1DD54FF4CF1D292C4996E95607ACA17F7A20B52C/[/img]

[h1]7. Black Dog Elite Pilots - Maziz[/h1][url=http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=733874292&searchtext=]LINK[/url]
We love a good pilot mod. This mod gives your soldier a Black Dog makeover, adding a black suit, and new goggles. Complete with a black dog patch, this mod will make you feel like a real pro when you play, and strike fear in to the heart of your enemies![img]http://images.akamai.steamusercontent.com/ugc/264969860598854936/2D113591419EA38E5A0C60E8B2DC6F0266EAC913/[/img]

[h1]6. Weapon Prototypes – Frenchox[/h1][url=http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=731545384&searchtext=]LINK[/url]
With over 15 prototype weapons this mod is a shed load of fun, including mortars that almost level an entire playing field, a state of the art Virus Vploader weapon (not a real virus!) and neon lazers! This mod was a personal favourite of a few players here and we look forward to seeing more of it![img]http://images.akamai.steamusercontent.com/ugc/269472527195862480/9F8E89F31DB89D1E454DA1375F1BD107D0707BA8/[/img]

[h1]5. Sphelx Komodo Wireframe Set – Sphelx Komodo[/h1][url=http://steamcommunity.com/id/sphelx/myworkshopfiles/?appid=301650]LINK[/url]
Harking back to the original Battlezone game, this funky mod turns the map into a green and black grid, as well as gives you a neon green tank and bomber to fly around in! For pure originality and the nostalgia trip, this gets a place in the top 5! We’re very much hoping for more of this...[img]http://images.akamai.steamusercontent.com/ugc/261591516979946108/317CE34C9C16495E4BB4A077ABEC534EFDC550CD/[/img]

[h1]4. Japanese Rocket Tank – Systeme[/h1][url=http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=734498779&searchtext=]LINK[/url]
Systeme did something we weren’t sure possible, created a new vehicle type. With an edited back section this new ship is a play on the American Rocket Tank, but with a Japanese makeover and a stylish new rear section. This has garnered a lot of attention in the forums, and we’re keen to see how he accomplished this feat. Hopefully this will start a new wave of vehicle mods! We’ll have t wait and see...[img]http://images.akamai.steamusercontent.com/ugc/261591516983561017/F6EA5C4C10BB717CAD291CC67576E8A9A418845D/[/img]

[h1]3. Advanced Combat Training – GeneralBlackDragon[/h1][url=http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=730880510&searchtext=]LINK[/url]
With a mod that has even taught some of the old dogs new tricks, the Advanced Combat Training mod has gained some serious praise from veteran modders, with some calling for it to be included as a stock training mission! notes.title: Battlezone 98 Redux expands with The Red Odyssey
notes.notes:
Battlezone 98 Redux is a new version of, you guessed it, Battlezone, the RTS-FPS mash-up that posited galactic warfare between the USA and its arch-nemesis, itself - sorry, its arch-nemesis, Russia. Now, the remake of that old game has been joined by a remake of its old expansion, The Red Odyssey. This adds two new campaigns set in the Jupiter region, along with a couple of new playable factions: the NSDF Black Dogs and the Chinese Red Army. Here's the trailer:

What's that, trailer? You say the expansion you're trailing has a 15% Steam discount, for the next few days? And you go on to say that the base game is currently 40% off, over the same period? Thanks, trailer.

A reminder that Rebellion - who now owns the rights to Battlezone, and who got Big Boat Interactive to develop this - is currently working on a reboot of the original, 1980 Battlezone. Although we haven't heard squat about that one for a while.

notes.title: Battlezone 98 Redux Mods Competition
notes.notes:

[b]Calling all Battlezone 98 Redux players! Whether you’re a mod master or a newbie (or you’ve never even tried modding!) we’re giving you the chance to WIN a brand new Toshiba gaming laptop, as well as a whole range of awesome prizes. All you have to do is show us your best mod![/b]


Here at Rebellion we love mods of all shapes and sizes, and our aim is to get more players to not only download mods, but create their own!

That’s why we’re offering awesome prizes to [b]5 LUCKY MODDERS[/b], including a brand new [b]Toshiba Gaming Laptop, AMD GPUs[/b] and [b]CPUs[/b], and [b]Rebellion Anthologies![/b] 

[h1]“Isn’t modding hard?”[/h1]
NOPE! For basic mods all you need is a little patience, a good knowledge of Windows Explorer and your favourite image editing software.

To help you get started we’ve created  some handy guides on building a custom skin and multiplayer map below:

    http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=713335452
    http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=665881032
[h1]So, what do I need to do?[/h1]
To be in with a chance of winning, we want you to create the best mod you possibly can, whether it’s a new skin for your favourite tank, a new HUD design, a new multiplayer map, an all new Instant Action (singleplayer) map or whatever you like! 
Then, simply upload it to the Steam workshop (or hosting website) before August 4th so that our expert Battlezone 98 Redux judges and moderators can have a play! 

[b]Full instructions can be found at the bottom of this page.[/b]
 
[h1]What are you and the judges looking for?[/h1]
We’re looking for a whole variety of mods, and we want to ensure that both modding masters and cadets are in with a chance of winning so we’ll be judging on many different levels! Some of the main things we’re looking for are:
[list]
    [*]How original is your idea?
    [*]How creative is your design?
    [*]Is it fun to play?
    [*]Does it add to the Battlezone universe or do something completely different?[/list]

[h1]Is there anywhere I can go for some modding help?[/h1]
The Battlezone 98 Redux forum on Steam is a great place for anyone who wants to mod! It’s full of helpful moderators who are always happy to chat (or maybe even test your mod out) and there’s a dedicated section for modding! There’s also a guide section, where you can read a number of guides on how to create and upload mods. 

We will also be browsing the forums and assisting players where we can, but if you’re really stuck, head over to our support page and send us a message and a member of our support team will get back to you as soon as they can!

[h1]Prizes[/h1]
[list]
   [*] [b]Grand Prize[/b]: AMD Gaming Laptop, A key for the Rebellion Anthology on Steam, Battlezone 98 Redux T-shirt + key for The Red Odyssey (on Steam OR GoG)
    [*][b]2nd Place[/b]: AMD GPU, A key for the Rebellion Anthology on Steam, Battlezone 98 Redux T-shirt + key for The Red Odyssey (on Steam OR GoG)
    [*][b]3rd Place[/b]: AMD CPU, A key for the Rebellion Anthology on Steam, Battlezone 98 Redux T-shirt + key for The Red Odyssey (on Steam OR GoG)

  [*] [b] 5th Place[/b]: A key for the Rebellion Anthology on Steam, Battlezone 98 Redux T-shirt + key for The Red Odyssey (on Steam OR GoG)[/list]

[b]Bonus awards[/b] – we’ll be giving away more keys and tees to plenty more mods that caught our eye, not just the best ones! 

[h1]How to submit your mod![/h1]
[b][u]Steam users[/u][/b]

To enter, you will need to upload your mod creation to the Steam workshop:
[list]
    [*]Once you have uploaded your mod to the workshop (this is explained at the end of our guides), add ‘Battlezone 98 Redux Mod Competition’ at the top of your description
    [*]Your description should help to explain exactly what your mod is and does!
    [*]Please also add the tag ‘ModComp16’[/list]

[h1]Terms & Conditions[/h1]
All entries must abide by the following Terms & Conditions. 
[list]
    [*]Rebellion reserves the right to cancel the competition at any time
    [*]Maximum of 1 prize tier can be won per person. You may enter as many mods as you like!.
    [*]Prizes are subject to change and availability Some prizes may not be suitable for certain ages. If you are under 18 we might need to substitute some prizes.
    [*]By submitting your entry to the contest you confirm that all work is your own and does not include trademarks, logos or copyright material not owned by the mod creator.
    [*]Your mod must work with Battlezone 98 Redux, and not dependant on other mods or external programs.
    [*]By submitting an entry, you give us permission to share your awesome work with the world in screenshots, videos, on our store pages and more! We may need to modify your work a little in order to do this, but we’ll ask your permission if we do!
    [*]Judging will completed by Rebellion as well as select members of the Battlezone 98 Redux community beta team. All Rebellion decisions will be final. Winners will be decided and announced after the 4th August closing date!
    [*]If a winner cannot be contacted or doesn’t claim their prize in a timely manner, we’ll give it to the next most suitable entry.[/list]

notes.title: BATTLEZONE 98 REDUX DEV BLOG 2
notes.notes:
[img]http://www.rebellion.co.uk/media/W1siZiIsIjIwMTYvMDQvMTUvMTVfMTRfNTZfMjMxX1RhbmtUZXguanBnIl0sWyJwIiwidGh1bWIiLCI2NDd4MzMzIyJdXQ/TankTex.jpg[/img]

[h1]Battlezone 98 fans... it's nearly here! [/h1]

[i][b]As we get closer and closer to the launch of Battlezone 98 Redux ,we're excited to continue our dev blog series as we delve deep into the remaster's development. Here, courtesy of producer Mike Arkin, is the second entry in the series, in which Mike talks about how his team have given Redux's models a thorough makeover. [/b][/i]

Hi, my name is Mike Arkin and I’m the producer of Battlezone 98 Redux. By strange coincidence, I was also a member of the original team that launched Battlezone in 1998. In this second dev diary I’m going to talk about what we did to enhance the art for Redux - specifically the vehicle and building models.

In 1998, the state-of-the-art in 3D games was very different to what it is today. Back then, the Grizzly tank was made up of about 300 polygons and it had a single texture that was 128 pixels by 128 pixels i.e. an 8-bit image! We thought it looked great at the time, but bear in mind that the average PC didn’t even have a 3D card back then and when they did, our target was a card with 4MB of ram. 4 megabytes! Yikes.

[h1]A GRIZZLY TRANSFORMATION[/h1]

Here is what that Grizzly looked like. Notice how rough the textures are and how, because the models have such low polygon counts, there is almost no detail - it’s all just flat.

[url=http://i.imgur.com/ltze484.jpg][img]http://i.imgur.com/ltze484.jpg[/img][/url]
[url=http://i.imgur.com/n7PIFEF.jpg][img]http://i.imgur.com/n7PIFEF.jpg[/img][/url]

Fast forward 17 years later and PCs are a just a little bit faster. And we really wanted to make Battlezone 98 Redux shine. So the first step was to remodel all the tanks at a much more reasonable level of detail, at around 8000-10,000 polygons in fact.  We actually used the original models as reference since it was important to us that the vehicles in game felt familiar. We wanted the same shape, but better looking.

We didn’t actually have the original models from scratch, but using a utility called NOESIS we were able to convert the cooked game assets back into a format called FBX. This meant we could use the exact models and textures as a basis for the new models.

So, here is the new Grizzly model. Notice we added lots of detail and rounded all the sharp edges a bit.  The tank barrel is no longer just a long rectangle as we gave it some flutes and an actual opening.

[url=http://i.imgur.com/Mb7Ue8G.jpg][img]http://i.imgur.com/Mb7Ue8G.jpg[/img][/url]

[h1]LET'S GET READY TO RUMBLE![/h1]

Once we did that, it was time for new textures.  With our minimum specifications just a bit upgraded from the 4MB days, we were able to redo the textures to match the new models.

The end result:  2048x2048 per vehicle with even larger textures for larger buildings

Here is the texture for the new Grizzly…

[url=http://i.imgur.com/gpJHjnG.jpg][img]http://i.imgur.com/gpJHjnG.jpg[/img][/url]

And here is the textured Grizzly …looking good, baby, ready for outer space war!

[url=http://i.imgur.com/GflcyWL.jpg][img]http://i.imgur.com/GflcyWL.jpg[/img][/url]

We really wanted to keep the look of the original tank through key elements like the star and eye decor.  We also wanted to retain the roughened, rugged look from the original game, which was very different then the super clean look of Battlezone 2.

But wait, there’s more! Video cards now have programmable shaders, and modern shaders can read multiple textures, so we didn’t just use a single texture like we did in the original game.

We added a few extra bits like a specular map to show where the vehicle should be shiny.

[url=http://i.imgur.com/u9W4see.jpg][img]http://i.imgur.com/u9W4see.jpg[/img][/url]

And a normal map, which helps to show the way light reflects.

[url=http://i.imgur.com/YzQYiSu.jpg][img]http://i.imgur.com/YzQYiSu.jpg[/img][/url]

And an emissive map, which shows where on the vehicle there is light being emitted.

[url=http://i.imgur.com/S1EumE5.jpg][img]http://i.imgur.com/S1EumE5.jpg[/img][/url]

The emissive map is great because now we can have things glow, and we’ve sure made a bunch of things glow. Once we saw it in action we wanted things to really pop, so we added a full screen shader to make all the emissive effects on screen have a super glow effect. 

Which, I think you’ll agree, looks superb.

[h1]THE FINAL RESULT[/h1]

So when you put it all together, you can see that our tanks (and buildings) look fantastic!

[url=http://i.imgur.com/fmqv5vr.jpg][img]http://i.imgur.com/fmqv5vr.jpg[/img][/url]

One of the other things we could do with these fancy new shaders was real-time shadowing, so now as you can see the tank has some nice fancy lighting which now includes-self shadowing.  If you don’t know the term, self shadowing means the light from the sun causes parts of the vehicles to cast shadows onto themselves.  So, for example, the tank gun casts a shadow onto the tank.

Even the old boxy pilot got a makeover!

[url=http://i.imgur.com/aKSX2Hx.jpg][img]http://i.imgur.com/aKSX2Hx.jpg[/img][/url]

He’s not just blessed with a high polygon count and a fancy new texture. Now he’s a skinned model with 18 animations.  That’s about 15 more than the original!

So there you go, high-poly models, fantastic textures and modern shaders, took us from here...

[url=http://i.imgur.com/n7PIFEF.jpg][img]http://i.imgur.com/n7PIFEF.jpg[/img][/url]

To here:

[url=http://i.imgur.com/GflcyWL.jpg][img]http://i.imgur.com/GflcyWL.jpg[/img][/url]

Not bad, right?

Thanks again for reading! We can’t wait to show you Battlezone 98 Redux very soon. As ever, if you have any questions or want more info, feel free on the Steam forums – I’d love to respond to you!

[i][b]Look out for more posts in the coming days, and make sure to stay tuned to Battlezone 98 Redux's [url=http://store.steampowered.com/app/301650/]Steam[/url] page and our [url=https://twitter.com/Rebellion]Twitter[/url] and [url=https://www.facebook.com/rebelliondevelopments]Facebook[/url] feeds for the latest news. 

Battlezone 98 Redux is coming to Steam this spring.[/b][/i]

Hi, my name is Mike Arkin and I’m the producer of Battlezone 98: Redux. By strange coincidence, I was also a member of the original team that launched Battlezone in 1998.

Since announcing Battlezone 98 Redux I’ve often been asked what a remaster means. While there is no one definition of a game remaster, I thought I’d use this first dev diary to explain what this remaster is.

Our high concept when we planned this project was to preserve the original gameplay, but enhance and augment the game in every way we could.  Keep in mind that we constantly struggle with the idea that we want to make the game as modern as possible, but we also need to service the fans that have been playing Battlezone for so many years and have kept the community alive. It’s hard to please everyone, but I’m pretty sure that most people will be happy with what we’ve done.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Bp57Lo2grfM

[h1]OUT WITH THE OLD, IN WITH THE NEW...[/h1]
So what did we do? Well, the short version is that we’re still working with the old engine, but we have ripped pieces out and replaced them with modern features.  Also, we’ve replaced most if not all of the art in the game with modern versions.  Some of the art looks similar to the original since we used all of the old art as reference, but when you put the two side by side the difference is clear.

We’ve not redesigned the game, though. Instead, we’ve strived to make the game we would have made in 1998 if PCs were 100 times more powerful back then, like they are now. In fact, based on some quick math, maybe perhaps 1000 is a better number (our minimum spec back in 1998 was a Pentium 90!).

[h1]LET THERE BE LIGHT...[/h1]
The longer version?  For starters, we introduced a shader-based DirectX 9 renderer which allowed us to use an all new shader/material system throughout the game. All vehicles and buildings were remodeled and retextured in high resolution and high polygon meshes. We also used advanced shader techniques to add a little glow and shine to the new models.

And what’s the point of shine if we don’t have lights? So of course we added headlights to all the tanks and adapted the system to allow for real-time lighting.

Speaking of lighting, we now have a real lighting system, and all game objects like vehicles and buildings cast shadows and self-shadow! You might be thinking that Battlezone had shadows in 1998, but really it just had blobs, not actual projected shadows with soft edges like Battlezone 98 Redux has.

[h1]HEADS UP![/h1]
The in-game heads-up display (HUD) was also completely redesigned. And we’ve made it scalable so at higher resolutions it looks nice and sharp. This also means that if you have a giant monitor you can now have your HUD scale up way high, or dial it back down if you’d prefer! Oh, and the Russian vehicles now have their own HUD, as do the mysterious Furies!

[img]http://i.imgur.com/1ylyEW5.jpg[/img]

Here is the stock HUD at 4x resolution (click for the full image)

[h1]EARTHSHATTERING ...[/h1]
One of the most interesting changes we made (and the subject of one of my next blogs) is the terrain.  Since Battlezone 98 Redux takes place in space on various barren planets, the terrain is really important since for many levels it’s most of what’s on screen.  Also, it makes up a very large percentage of a user generated level, so it was vital to make the new terrain compatible with old maps.  

So we rewrote the terrain system, cranked up the mesh to four times the current resolution, did a little shader magic to eliminate seams, added specular and normal maps to keep things interesting, and we added a detail texture to all the terrain tiles.  The end result is terrain that is the same size and shape of the original terrain, but so much better looking. 

[img]http://i.imgur.com/nEqAkYG.jpg[/img]

Check out that terrain! (click for full image) 

[h1]BACK TO THE FUTURE[/h1]
And, since we retained compatibility with all of the old file formats, all the user generated maps created over the years can go through a five-minute conversion process and run in Battlezone 98 Redux with upgraded assets. When an old map is loaded Battlezone 98 Redux takes care of upscaling and smoothing automatically, so it’s easy and quick to convert and modernize any map.  

Speaking of which, back in 1998 we shipped the game with the tools we used to make the game. Crude tools, sure, but they were good enough that a healthy map and mod community grew over 17 years! 

Well, Battlezone 98: Redux goes one step further by adding Steam Workshop support and a host of in-game options for pulling your new content into the game and running it.  No longer do you need to edit text files to add a MP map; now the map is recognized and will be displayed in-game, ready to play!  No longer do you need to load Instant Action missions from the command line; now all of your IA missions are displayed in a menu ready to load with a few mouse clicks! And for game mods, there is now a Mod menu where you can activate and deactivate mods simply and easily.

[img]http://i.imgur.com/8SwfGcK.jpg[/img]

Here is the Mod selection screen with four mods loaded and active (click for full image) 

In fact, there’s a dedicated group of map makers that have already converted maps and loaded them onto Steam Workshop so they are ready to go! So yes, when we launch Battlezone 98 Redux there will be plenty of content available on Steam Workshop, day 1.

These are the highlights of what’s new in Battlezone 98 Redux, but there are a host of other changes and improvements to the game which I’ll cover in future blog posts. Things like multiplayer, bug and AI fixes, menus and fonts. I’ll also get into some of the more detailed specifics of the vehicles, terrains and so on. Until then, thanks for reading and for your continued support of Battlezone 98 Redux. We can’t wait to finally show you the finished game very soon. If you have questions or want more info, feel free to post on the Steam forums – I’d love to respond to you!

[i][b]Look out for more posts in the coming days, and make sure to stay tuned to the Battlezone 98 Redux's [url=http://store.steampowered.com/app/301650/]Steam[/url] page and our [url=https://twitter.com/Rebellion]Twitter[/url] and [url=https://www.facebook.com/rebelliondevelopments]Facebook[/url] feeds for the latest news. Battlezone 98 Redux is coming to Steam this spring...[/b][/i]

notes.title: Rebellion reveals Battlezone 98 Redux
notes.notes:
In addition to the VR Battlezone reboot Rebellion announced last summer, Battlezone 98 Redux, a remake of the 1998 version of Battlezone that was developed by Activision (which as Wikipedia explains bears little resemblance to the original"), is in the works. 

Both Game Rankings and MobyGames indicate that it received a very positive critical response, including a 93 percent review score from yours truly (in the magazine, of course, as this was 18 years ago). While the original game's fiction, as far as I can remember, didn't get much beyond tanks in space, Battlezone 98 Redux is set in an alt-history 1960s, in which the space race has led to a shooting war between the US and the USSR over mysterious alien bio-metals.

Battlezone 98 Redux will blend first-person combat with real-time strategy, featuring remastered visuals, online multiplayer, and near unlimited mod content from Steam Workshop. There will be two separate single-player campaigns, one American and one Soviet, comprised of 29 missions spread across seven different planetary environments, as well as Deathmatch and Strategy online modes for two to eight players.

The system requirements:

The Little Willie:

  • OS: Windows XP, Windows Vista, Windows 7, Windows 8 or Windows 10
  • Processor: Dual-core CPU with SSE3 (Intel Pentium D 3GHz / AMD Athlon™ 64 X2 4200) or better
  • Memory: 2 GB RAM
  • Graphics: Microsoft DirectX 10.0 compatible graphics card with 256 MB of memory (NVIDIA GeForce 8800 series / ATI Radeon™ HD 2600 Pro) or better
  • Storage: 2 GB available space
  • Sound Card: Microsoft DirectX 10.0 compatible sound card or better

The Challenger 2:

  • OS: Windows 7, Windows 8 or Windows 10
  • Processor: Intel Core™ i5 / AMD FX series or better
  • Memory: 6 GB RAM
  • Graphics: Microsoft DirectX 11.0 compatible graphics card with 1GB of memory (NVIDIA GeForce 400 series / ATI Radeon™ HD 7750) or better
  • Storage: 2 GB available space
  • Sound Card: Microsoft DirectX 10.0 compatible sound card or better

Battlezone 98 Redux is slated for launch in the spring. You can find out more at battlezone98.com.

Edit: This article originally conflated Rebellion's VR Battlezone with Battlezone 98 Redux. They are, in fact, two different games.

notes.title: BATTLEZONE 98 REDUX LAUNCHES SPRING 2016
notes.notes:
[img]http://i.imgur.com/8nqZrt9.png?1[/img]
Rebellion are delighted to reveal much anticipated remaster of Battlezone (1998) - one of the greatest sci-fi strategy titles ever made (in our opinion)!

[url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Bp57Lo2grfM] Watch the Battlezone 98 Redux reveal trailer [/url]

Launching on Steam for PC this Spring, Battlezone 98 Redux keeps the core rush of first-person action and RTS gameplay that earned widespread critical acclaim, and blends it with remastered visuals, online multiplayer and the potential for near limitless new content with support for Steam Workshop mods!

[h1]Made by devs from the original Battlezone (1998)[/h1]
As lots of you reading this will know, Battlezone (1998)’s revolutionary gameplay fostered a really strong community that still develops mods for the game to this day.

To ensure Battlezone 98 Redux remained faithful to the community, we enlisted the developers at Big Boat Interactive, who include three developers from the 1998 Battlezone game and played a key part in keeping the community alive for 18 years.

We’re going to let Mike and the Big Boat guys loose on these community pages very soon, so watch out!

[h1]Rebellion’s first externally developed title[/h1]
Hiring Big Boat Interactive to develop Battlezone 98 Redux marks another significant milestone for Rebellion too!

Since we self-published the PC editions of Sniper Elite V2 and Sniper Elite 3 games, Rebellion has changed from “just” being a games studio, to being one of the UK’s largest indie studio and publisher with the multi-format retail release of Zombie Army Trilogy in 2015 for PC, Xbox One and PlayStation 4.

Battlezone 98 Redux represents a new chapter in this journey, the first in a series of Rebellion IP to be developed out-of-house as our internal teams continue to crack on with Battlezone for PlayStation VR, and more unannounced “AAA” titles.

So for now, thank you for your support and we hope you’re as excited for Battlezone 98 Redux as we are!
[img]http://i.imgur.com/9TZFYot.png[/img]
